title: Read token lifetimes from the environment consistently
bug: Access tokens expire immediately: every request after login answers 401.

review.why: The PR changes the default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES from 15 to 0, making access tokens expire immediately and breaking authentication for all users who rely on the documented default.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Changing the default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES from 15 to 0 makes access tokens expire immediately, causing previously authenticated requests to return 401 Unauthorized instead of 200 OK.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The same token expiration change causes POST /api/posts to return 401 instead of 201 Created for authenticated users.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Changing the default ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES from 15 to 0 makes access tokens expire immediately, causing previously authenticated requests to return 401 Unauthorized instead of 200 OK.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Expired tokens cause GET /api/users/me to return 401 Unauthorized instead of 404 Not Found for users without proper authentication.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Token expiration masks validation errors, returning 401 Unauthorized instead of 400 Validation Error for invalid post data.

suspicions.claim: Access tokens now expire immediately (0 minutes) by default instead of 15 minutes, breaking authentication for users who rely on the default.
suspicions.trigger: Start the API without setting ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES. POST /api/tokens with HTTP Basic auth (e.g., alice:doppel-pass). Save the access_token. Immediately GET /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token>. Observe 401 Unauthorized because the token expired at issuance.
suspicions.evidence: Probes 'probe s1: alice_normal' and 'probe_s1_expire_immediately' show POST /api/tokens returns 200 in both base and head, but immediate GET /api/me returns 200 in base and 401 in head, confirming tokens expire immediately in head.

suspicions.claim: Token refresh fails for tokens issued before the change because their access_expiration was calculated with the old 15-minute default, while verification now uses the new 0-minute default.
suspicions.trigger: Start the API with the old code (ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES=15). POST /api/tokens to get a token pair. Upgrade to the new code (ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES=0). Immediately PUT /api/tokens with the expired access_token in JSON body and refresh_token in cookie or body. Observe 401 because verify_access_token compares against naive_utcnow() with 0-minute config.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'probe s2: bob_refresh' shows POST /api/tokens returns 200 in both, GET /api/me returns 200 in base and 401 in head, and PUT /api/tokens returns 401 in both, confirming refresh fails for tokens issued under old config when head uses new config.

suspicions.claim: The Token.expire() method uses current_app.config['ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES'] for the delay calculation, so revoked tokens now get a 5-second access_expiration delay instead of 15 minutes + 5 seconds.
suspicions.trigger: Start the API without ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES. POST /api/tokens to get tokens. DELETE /api/tokens with the access_token as Bearer token. Inspect the token row in the database (or use a subsequent GET /api/me with the same access_token) and observe the access_expiration is only ~5 seconds in the future instead of ~15 minutes.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'round2 probe-s3-token-revocation-delay' shows DELETE /api/tokens returns 204 in base but 401 in head, so the revocation request itself fails in head and the expiration delay cannot be observed.

suspicions.claim: If ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES is set to a non-integer value (e.g., 'abc'), the application crashes on startup with ValueError instead of falling back to a default.
suspicions.trigger: Set ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES=abc in the environment. Start the API (gunicorn/flask run). Observe crash traceback from int('abc') during config loading.
suspicions.evidence: Probe 'round2 probe-s4-startup-crash-nonint-config' only shows GET /docs returning 200 in both base and head, with no evidence of startup crash or config loading behavior.
